text: Closed-shell HF for H₂: independent references, SCF residuals and basis refinement Solve two-electron H₂ at fixed proton positions using original s-Gaussian integrals and restricted closed-shell Hartree–Fock (RHF). Energy stabilization, satisfaction of the discrete SCF equations, changes under basis expansion and physical accuracy are separate questions. This implementation covers isolated two-electron H2 RHF in finite s-only bases. It does not implement general molecular HF, establish a complete-basis limit, recover the correlated dissociation curve, or supply molecular/periodic DFT. On this page The model being solved This is a Born–Oppenheimer electronic problem with the internuclear distance R fixed by the input. Atomic units are used: distances in bohr and energies in hartree. Relativistic effects, nuclear motion, vibration/rotation, solvent and periodic boundaries are excluded. Total energy including nuclear repulsion 1/R is recorded separately from electronic energy. The two electrons occupy the same spatial orbital with opposite spins in closed-shell RHF. The same restriction is retained at stretched geometries. SCF convergence and agreement with another implementation do not establish the correct dissociation limit or recover electron correlation. J. (1951), C. A. Coulson and I. Fischer (1949) Gaussian basis functions and original integrals Normalized s-type Gaussians centered on the two nuclei form the basis. A contracted function combines several exponents and coefficients, with normalization also applied to the contraction. Three primitives in STO-3G describe one contracted s function, not three independent basis functions. Inputs and results retain exponents, coefficients and contractions. The STO-3G numerical convention is checked against Basis Set Exchange version 1, rather than presented as a direct transcription of the original paper’s printed digits. The educational code computes overlap S, kinetic T, nuclear attraction V and electron-repulsion integrals, defining the one-electron matrix as h=T+V. The s-type Coulomb integrals involve the Boys function F₀, which tends to 1 as t approaches zero. Direct evaluation of erf(√t)/√t at zero would produce 0/0, so the limiting region needs a stable treatment. Pople (1969), Basis Set Exchange (2018) How SCF convergence is judged Symmetric orthogonalization converts the Roothaan equation to an ordinary eigenproblem. Occupied orbitals define a new density, which rebuilds the Fock matrix for the next iteration. Density mixing can stabilize iterations, but an intermediate mixed density need not satisfy the idempotency condition of a pure determinant. Final density, orbitals and Fock matrix are therefore checked in a consistent state. A small energy change alone is insufficient. Energy change, the Frobenius norm of the AO-density change and the Frobenius norm of the orthonormal-coordinate commutator residual are compared with input thresholds. Orbital orthogonality, electron count Tr(PS)=2 and closed-shell idempotency PSP=2P are also measured. The matrix-trace energy with F[P] rebuilt from the final density is compared with a separate occupied-orbital/electron-repulsion-integral reconstruction. The minimum overlap eigenvalue and condition number are recorded. Near-linear dependence makes S⁻¹ᐟ² amplify errors. Termination reasons and iteration limits are explicit; reaching the limit is not reported as convergence. A stationary solution also need not be a stable minimum, so residual checks do not replace a full RHF/UHF stability analysis. C. J. (1951), PySCF developers (2026) Basis refinement and its limits SCF tolerance controls the remaining solution error within one fixed basis. A basis change changes the discrete problem itself. Basis comparisons retain tight SCF settings, geometry, nuclear repulsion and the RHF constraint. True RHF minima in nested variational spaces cannot increase in energy under expansion. Switching to a different local stationary branch would invalidate that simple comparison. Refinement here is limited to the finite s-only sequence defined by the public input. Adjacent-basis energy changes are measured, but the absence of p and higher angular functions means this does not prove convergence to the complete-basis-set (CBS) limit or chemical accuracy. Unrelated basis sets and different contractions are not all treated as a nested sequence. For each separation, the final two additions are checked against the stated energy-change target. This is a stopping diagnostic for the published sequence, not an upper bound on true basis error. The tolerance sweep changes only SCF thresholds and compares with a tighter solution. The basis sweep keeps SCF settings aligned. These differences and independent-implementation differences are separate outputs. A small final basis increment does not eliminate physical approximation error. (1951) Independent reference and reproduction The reference script supplies the same geometry, charge, spin and explicit Gaussian basis to PySCF, using its independent integral library and SCF procedure for RHF energies. It does not call the educational integral, Fock or SCF functions. Both calculations solve the same physical model in the same finite basis; the comparison is not against an exact correlated energy. The release records input/reference hashes, dependency versions, total energies, reference differences, iteration histories and termination reasons. Extract the ZIP into another directory and run the same fixed input, checking residual/error values against criteria as well as the JSON pass flag. Regenerating the independent reference is separate from ordinary reruns using the saved reference. Sources: Qiming Sun et al. (2020), PySCF developers (2026) Reading the stored measurements These values come from the release’s fixed inputs. Inputs and JSON retain thresholds, stopping rules and complete iteration histories.
